Steps: install plugin/checkout at pinned commit; start local Milvus (make up); export OPENAI_API_KEY for the openai embedding provider; index each of three sizes into its own collection; flush; verify chunk counts against an independent Milvus count(*). External accounts: 1 (OpenAI, for text-embedding-3-small). Credentials: 2 (OPENAI_API_KEY, plus Milvus URI which is unauthenticated locally). Failed attempt 1: memsearch CLI runs with cwd set to the plugin checkout, so relative corpus paths fail with 'Path does not exist' -- loud, fixed by passing absolute paths. Failed attempt 2 was SILENT and is the significant one: see silent_failures.

After 'Indexed 52 chunks.' (rc=0), every search returned 'No results found.' / [] with rc=0 and no error, on a collection Milvus reported 52 rows for. Cause: memsearch store.search() guards BM25 against empty collections by testing get_collection_stats()['row_count'], and Milvus derives that count from SEALED SEGMENTS ONLY -- freshly inserted, unflushed data reads as 0. An explicit flush makes the same query return results immediately. A user who indexed and searched in one session would conclude the tool does not work, or worse, that their history contains nothing. NOTE: this is the SAME failure mode WS6a recorded for claude-context (finding 3: get_collection_stats returns row_count 0 for a freshly-indexed collection because stats lag unflushed inserts) -- two independently built retrieval tools making the identical mistake of treating Milvus segment stats as a liveness signal.
